summary: The probe gate scans only five hard-coded files, but project.yml compiles every file under Sources/, so extra Swift files are never checked.
failure_scenario: Add ios-probe/Sources/Extra.swift containing AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setCategory(.playAndRecord) and a second LocalAudioTrack.createTrack(name:) call. REQUIRED_FILES (lines 9-15) does not list it. The forbidden-API patterns (lines 74-76) and the exactly-one-microphone-track check (line 81) therefore never see it, and the gate prints 'passed'. The probe would build with a parallel audio-session owner or a second mic track.
evidence: Copied ios-probe to the scratchpad, added Sources/Extra.swift with both violations, and ran scripts/validate_probe.py. It printed 'VPIO probe structural gate passed' and exited 0. project.yml sources: [Sources] compiles every file in the directory.

summary: Version, deployment-target and API-marker checks are substring tests over raw text, so a YAML comment, the README or a Swift comment satisfies them while the real value differs.
failure_scenario: Set exactVersion: "2.16.0" # exactVersion: "2.15.3" in project.yml. Line 59 only tests `'exactVersion: "2.15.3"' in project`, so the pin gate still passes with LiveKit unpinned from 2.15.3. Required markers (lines 17-30, 83-96) are satisfied by comments or string literals in the same way, e.g. a '// guard case .applied = result' comment. Lines 66-70 also include README.md in the scanned text.
evidence: Edited the scratchpad copy of project.yml as above; validate_probe.py still exited 0. The markers appear only in ProbeModel.swift, and grep shows no code-vs-comment distinction in the script.

summary: Nothing runs validate_probe.py: it is not referenced from .github, docs, scripts, pyproject.toml or any test.
failure_scenario: The README and project pin can drift or a forbidden API can be added, and no CI or test notices. The structural gate exists only on paper.
evidence: Ran `grep -rn 'ios-probe\|ios_probe\|validate_probe'` over .github, docs, scripts, tests, pyproject.toml and README.md. Only the file itself matched.

summary: The acquisition worker computes CRC32C with a pure-Python bit loop at about 1.2 MB/s, but the catalog allows a 1 GiB closure under a 600 s worker timeout.
failure_scenario: _download_resource (line 155) CRCs every 1 MiB chunk in Python. At the measured throughput, 1 GiB of resources (the bound at worker line 113 / catalog _MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) needs about 890 s of CRC alone, which exceeds timeout_milliseconds=600_000 (qualification_moonshine_preparation.py:346). Even a 500 MB closure plus download time is marginal. The run then fails as a tool timeout that looks like an environment fault. The host repeats the same loop for all 9 resources in _verify_resource (preparation:221) and on every _prepared_resource_bytes call.
evidence: Timed _crc32c over 1 MiB on this host: 0.85 s (1.24 MB/s); known-answer check for '123456789' is 0xE3069283. The 600 s limit and 1 GiB bound are read from source. The real Moonshine catalog sizes were not fetched and no Windows end-to-end run was done, so the time-out itself is not reproduced.

summary: snapshot_regular_tree walks with os.walk and no onerror, so an unreadable subdirectory is silently skipped and its contents are missing from the 'unchanged' proof.
failure_scenario: A protected root (default root, active profile, evidence root, wheelhouse) contains a subdirectory the runner cannot list (ACL or permission). os.walk swallows the scandir error, the directory is still recorded as an entry (line 276), but nothing beneath it is hashed. A child that modifies files in that subtree passes require_tree_unchanged and the 'defaultRootUnchanged' and 'evidenceRootUnchanged' predicates. The same pattern is in the embedded _ENABLE_CHILD tree() (line 1566). In qualify_evidence_slice_zero.py, Path.rglob in the wheelhouse and Chrome completeness checks (lines 1008, 1166) also skips unreadable directories, so an unlisted wheel or file inside one is not seen.
evidence: As an unprivileged user, built tree/a/secret (mode 000, containing g) and tree/b/f, then ran snapshot_regular_tree. Keys returned: ['.', 'a/', 'a/secret/', 'b/', 'b/f'] with no error and no entry for a/secret/g. Reproduced on POSIX only. Windows ACL behavior is expected to match because os.walk's error handling is platform-independent, but it was not run on Windows.

summary: The delete qualification passes the literal "0.21.0" to installed_hermes_identity, so the recorded Hermes version is asserted, not observed.
failure_scenario: Every sibling gate (continuity, voice_archive, voice_archive_path) reads the version from the running Hermes. Here the version field of the evidence and of the `baseline` equality is a constant. If the checkout at the pinned commit reported a different __version__, the evidence would still claim 0.21.0 and baseline would still be True. The commit is verified, so the practical risk is low, but the field is a claim, not a measurement.
evidence: Read the call site and real_gate_support.installed_hermes_identity (identity = {'version': version, 'commit': HEAD}; baseline = identity == HERMES_BASELINE). qualify_voice_review.py:414 has the same literal but is outside this slice.

summary: The report validator rejects any PID that appears with two creation times anywhere in the report, which a valid multi-scenario run can produce through Windows PID recycling.
failure_scenario: Scenario 3 runs a process that gets PID 1234 after scenario 2's earlier process with PID 1234 exited (its Job is finalized and handles closed). Each (pid, creationFiletime) pair is unique and correct, but creation_by_pid.setdefault(...) at 1611-1615 fails with 'PID was reused with a different creation identity'. A genuine qualification report is then refused as invalid. Windows recycles PIDs quickly, and a run spawns many processes across 19 Jobs, so the intermittent failure is plausible.
evidence: Static reading only: the check is keyed on pid alone across all Jobs while seen_identities (1608) already enforces unique (pid, creation) pairs. No Windows run or synthetic report was built, so this was not demonstrated.

summary: The process-tree validator only rejects a child that predates its parent (`>`), so a parent cycle between two descendants with equal creation FILETIMEs passes.
failure_scenario: A forged report lists descendants A and B in one Job, each naming the other as parent with identical creationFiletime and a valid process group. Every per-process check passes, the root exists, and reachability to the root is never verified.
evidence: Static reading of _validate_topology_semantics_v1 (lines 1604-1642). No synthetic report was run.
